For a noncircular elliptic billiard with a strictly nested nondegenerate confocal elliptical caustic, the product of ordinary distances from all vertices to either fixed focus is independent of phase if and only if the primitive least period is congruent to 2 modulo 4. The result covers all admissible primitive star turns and both orientations. For every even least period, the two focal products are equal at each phase. Repetitions raise the positive primitive product to an integer power, so listed return length alone is insufficient. Circles are treated separately; hyperbolic and degenerate caustics are excluded.

This research note proves the primitive interpretation of the experimentally recorded invariant k114 in Reznik–Garcia–Koiller (2020/2021), establishes the exact period classification, and gives an exact doubled-triangle counterexample to the unrestricted six-event return interpretation. It applies Stachel's published parametrization, classical Jacobi identities and established meromorphic divisor methods. No new-method or exclusive historical priority claim is made. The bounded primary-source audit found no explicit earlier proof of this exact target; novelty of the specific formulation is not certified. Explicit fixed-binary-alphabet consequences of OpenAI's two relation-liveness lower bounds. A strict h-squared adjacency-block language has a one-way nondeterministic source with (3h^3-h)/2+2 endmarked states, and an ordinary epsilon-free source with one fewer state. Equivalent two-way deterministic automata and two-way nondeterministic automata for its full binary complement require 2^Omega(h), hence 2^Omega(n^(1/3)) in the cubic source size. The note gives exact transitions, an sh^2-state pullback, all-word complement semantics, and an h^3 fooling-set source lower bound. The exponential obstructions are inherited from OpenAI; binary coding is established machinery, attributed to earlier work. AI tools were used extensively. We prove the k307 outer-side pedal area-centroid observation of Reznik, Garcia and Koiller for billiards in a noncircular ellipse with a strict confocal elliptic caustic and least even period. The ordered perpendicular feet of any fixed point on the boundary tangent lines have an explicit phase-independent signed area centroid wherever their signed area is nonzero. We classify the entire zero-area locus: none when d is nonnegative, and a fixed circle when d is negative. Simple winding-one even families have a centroid for every fixed point; the four-period value is M/3. An exact primitive eight-period star shows that the exceptional undefined locus is real. The note supplies an all-period support-coordinate and cubic-moment proof. The verification archive contains the LaTeX source, exact symbolic and rational certificates, independent high-precision orbit controls, audit reports and reproducibility instructions. The original observation and classical methods are credited. Bounded primary-source audits found no earlier covering proof, without certifying historical firstness. An expanded consequence and verification note for OpenAI's rank-100 fixed-price construction. A self-contained regular-tree and cellular-boundary calculation proves that its displayed 101-generator/100-relator presentation complex is a finite two-dimensional classifying space and every L2-Betti number vanishes, independently of either cost bound. Gaboriau's action invariance and OpenAI's positive Bernoulli cost estimate then give an explicit free ergodic p.m.p. orbit relation with Cost at least 1 + 1/(100*2^61) and vanishing L2-Betti numbers. The group infimum cost is one.

The group and positive cost estimate are due to OpenAI; cost--Betti comparison and action invariance are due to Gaboriau. The general fixed-price implication was already explicit in Popa--Shlyakhtenko--Vaes, and the short conditional limit argument was already in the author's public preliminary triage. We give an explicit restriction and transference consequence of OpenAI's full annular variation theorem for the triangular Hilbert transform, manuscript dated October 5, 2026, at source commit adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a. For arbitrary commuting invertible probability-preserving transformations S,T and complex f,g in L3, the symmetric sums H_N=sum_(0<|n|<=N) f(S^n x)g(T^n x)/n, with H_0=0, satisfy a pointwise r-variation estimate in L^(3/2) for every r>2. They have a bounded maximum and converge almost everywhere and in L^(3/2), with maximal-tail convergence in that norm. The proof uses fixed positive-area cell boxes, half-integer radial endpoints, an explicitly summable O(k^-2) signed kernel error, and finite-menu finite-window Calderon transference. The continuous analytic breakthrough is inherited and credited; this note supplies its discrete restriction and ergodic consequence. Classical transference and its modern predecessors are credited, and no first-priority or independent triangular-Hilbert breakthrough claim is made. Scope remains L3 inputs, symmetric odd truncations, commuting transformations and r>2; there is no r=2, noncommuting or one-sided Cesaro claim. AI tools were used extensively in research, drafting and verification. Automated adversarial audits are not human peer review or formal certification. The relevant Lean artifacts concern an older maximal theorem and do not formally verify full annular variation or this note. For every prime p greater than 3 and every n at least 3, this research note constructs a finite flat commutative group scheme over W(closure of F_p), killed by p and of rank p^(2n), with quasi-supersingular special fiber, such that both the special fiber and its Witt-ring lift fail Cartier self-duality. It gives an explicit negative answer to the higher-rank question following Proposition 2 on page 2479 of Naotake Takao's contribution to Oberwolfach Report 42/2023.

The proof uses an explicit six-dimensional Dieudonne module, a supersingular elliptic p-torsion filtration, an image-intersection invariant and a finite Honda complement. These are applications of established Dieudonne and finite Honda theory, with the classical cyclic-word framework credited. No first-discovery or first-priority claim is made. For an arbitrary antimorphic involution theta, a finite word with alternating theta-periods p and q and length at least p+q-gcd(p,q) has alternating theta-period gcd(p,q). This proves the exact unnumbered conjecture after Theorem 23 on printed page 2220 of Nowotka's contribution, joint with Bischoff, to the 2010 Oberwolfach mini-workshop on combinatorics on words. The common finite extension theta(w)w has ordinary periods 2p and 2q; classical Fine-Wilf and central reflection give the alternating conclusion. A reversal example shows that the sufficient formula cannot be reduced by one uniformly; pairwise optimality is not asserted. The research note credits Fine and Wilf, the originating report and Bischoff's thesis, and compares the related Czeizler-Kari-Seki, Kari-Seki and Simpson results. Every positive definite real homogeneous form of positive degree admits an invertible real linear change of variables in which the symmetric ordered coefficients have diagonal entries equal to one and every mixed entry strictly between zero and one. This gives an affirmative answer to Brandes's Problem 11 in the 2019 Oberwolfach report on Analytic Number Theory, including the printed absolute-value inequality.

The three-page proof clusters a basis near a direction minimizing the form on a Euclidean sphere. A polynomial gap has a strictly positive quadratic term for every mixed tuple. The accompanying source package includes an independent proof via positive definite bilinear slices and Cauchy-Schwarz, internal adversarial audits including three fresh preprint-readiness rounds and independently rechecked supplementary controls, a dated priority search, and a standard-library Python verifier with exact rational certificates. The finite checks supplement the analytic proof and are not a formal verification of the universal theorem.

Brandes's 2015 discussion of pseudo-diagonal forms is credited as a direct precursor. A bounded literature audit found no earlier full resolution; first priority is not established. This is an unrefereed preprint developed and checked with generative-AI assistance. Paper and prose: CC BY 4.0. Code: MIT.

For each fixed genus g ≥ 1, let S(g,1) be an oriented compact surface with one boundary component, and let maps and isotopies fix that boundary pointwise. We prove that ordered positive factorizations of one positive boundary Dehn twist, along non-null-homotopic simple closed curves with repetitions permitted and pairwise geometric intersection at most one, have finitely many simultaneous-conjugacy classes. Their maximal length M(g) is finite and attained, with M(g) ≥ 4g(2g+1). Peripheral factors occur only in the singleton factorization; otherwise all factors are nonseparating. The values M(1) = 12 and M(2) = 40 are credited deductions from prior work with the convention bridge stated. This gives a complete negative answer, under the stated conventions, to the separately printed restricted arbitrary-length clause in the Wajnryb/Farb problem collection. The full original maximum and classification bundle remains partial: exact M(g) for g ≥ 3, explicit upper formulas, an effective exhaustive-enumeration stopping criterion, extremizers, and Hurwitz, positive Artin, T-move and A5/D6 classifications remain unresolved in this work. The note is a credited deduction and exposition. Cossu and Tringali's arXiv:2208.05869v3, Corollary 4.13, supplies the generic finite-alphabet finiteness corollary through a normal reduced cone and nonerasing atomic expansions. The support and ribbon arguments explicitly build on Juvan–Malnič–Mohar, Malestein–Rivin–Theran, and Cahn–Fanoni–Petri. Honda–Kazez–Matić, Smith, the chain relation, and Baykur–Monden–Van Horn-Morris provide credited premises.
